items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: He told me one time George Gershwin was his copyist

ctx.x: Scored in ink. And he told us that. And he taught me about scoring. He said, 'When you score, score four bars and then check it.' Check every note to see it's right. You see, this is how you keep from making mistakes. And he told me he used to give his copyists a dollar for every mistake he made, otherwise he would tell his copyists to copy everything they saw on the score -- don't be changing nothin' he wrote on the score. And he was right. I'd never seen nobody score in ink.
He told me one time George Gershwin was his copyist, when he was doing the Ziegfield shows.
And that stuff sounded so good, man.
